nodes.name: Mountain avens
nodes.desc: A small evergreen shrub of limestone outcrops. In the Burren it grows beside Mediterranean plants, a mix of arctic-alpine and southern flora.

nodes.name: Bloody crane's-bill
nodes.desc: A magenta-flowered perennial of the limestone grassland and pavement, among the most recorded plants in the area.

nodes.name: Bird's-foot-trefoil
nodes.desc: A low yellow-flowered legume of short grassland. Butterflies and bumblebees take its nectar.

nodes.name: Mother of thyme
nodes.desc: A creeping, aromatic herb of thin limestone soils that flowers in the short turf.

nodes.name: Hazel
nodes.desc: A shrub that spreads as scrub where grazing has declined. Its nuts feed squirrels and small rodents.

nodes.name: Native beef cattle
nodes.desc: Hardy cattle are traditionally grazed on the uplands from October to April (winterage). This keeps scrub down and the flower-rich turf open.

nodes.name: Feral goat
nodes.desc: Free-living goats roam the Burren uplands and browse its plants and shrubs.

nodes.name: European rabbit
nodes.desc: A grazer of short turf and an important prey animal for foxes, stoats, badgers and pine martens.

nodes.name: Wood mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed and fruit eater and prey for almost every predator in the web.

nodes.name: Red squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats hazel nuts and seeds. Wikipedia says pine martens help red squirrels by suppressing invasive grey squirrels.

nodes.name: Meadow brown
nodes.desc: The most recorded insect in the area. The adult feeds on flower nectar such as thyme.

nodes.name: Common carder bee
nodes.desc: A bumblebee that feeds on nectar and pollen from many flowers, including bird's-foot-trefoil and devil's-bit scabious.

nodes.name: Common frog
nodes.desc: An amphibian that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Otters, foxes, badgers and hedgehogs are all recorded eating frogs.

nodes.name: European hedgehog
nodes.desc: An insect-eating mammal that also takes frogs.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small mustelid hunter of rabbits, mice and voles.

nodes.name: European badger
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats small mammals, frogs and bumblebees among other foods.

nodes.name: European pine marten
nodes.desc: The Burren is one of its strongholds in Ireland. It eats small mammals, frogs, insects, berries and carrion.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A generalist predator of rabbits, rodents and frogs that also eats carrion.

nodes.name: Limestone pavement
nodes.desc: Bare limestone covers much of the uplands; the cracks hold ferns and flowers and the thin soil suits low specialist plants.

nodes.name: Atlantic rain
nodes.desc: Wet Atlantic weather feeds the plants of the thin soils and the Burren's seasonal lakes.

nodes.name: Mild winters
nodes.desc: The Atlantic coast climate is mild, one reason arctic-alpine and southern plants can grow side by side.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil life
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.
